title: Back online, new gym plans and trainer measurements can take up to 10 minutes to appear
what: The app counts a check with the gym as done before it knows the answer. If the phone was offline or the server failed, the Workout tab and the Body page will not ask again for 10 minutes. Only a pull-down on the Gym tab forces a new check.
expected: A check that failed is not counted, so the next screen open after the internet returns asks the gym again.
who: members of a gym on the trainer plan
how_often: each time the internet drops near a screen open
fix_line: Only mark a gym check as done once the gym has answered

title: When the gym server fails, the gym's workout of the day just disappears and gym plans stay old, with no word
what: If MettleUp's server is down or slow, the workout of the day card is not shown at all on a new day, and gym plans and diet plans silently stay at the last copy. The member is never told that the gym could not be reached, so they cannot tell 'no workout today' from 'could not check'.
expected: A short line such as 'Could not reach your gym, showing what we had' when the answer is old or missing.
who: members of a gym on the trainer plan
fix_line: Tell the member when the gym's answer could not be fetched

title: When the AI-written finish note fails, no note is kept of why
what: The opt-in AI finish note drops every failure without a word or a log line, so a retired AI model or a wrong key looks exactly like 'no note today'. This is the same way a past AI provider retired its models and nobody noticed.
expected: Each failure writes one log line with the reason, as the rest of the app does.
who: members who turned on AI coach notes (feature is behind a switch)
fix_line: Log the reason before falling back to the plain note

title: The one-time fix of imported workout times can run twice and move workouts by hours
what: The start-up fix that moves old imported workout times is not safe to repeat: a second run shifts the same workouts again. Its only guard is a saved 'done' mark, and if reading that mark fails, the app treats it as 'not done' and runs the fix again.
expected: A failed read of the 'done' mark skips the fix for now instead of running it again.
who: members who imported from Hevy or Strong
how_often: rare: only when the phone fails to read one saved setting
fix_line: When the done mark cannot be read, skip the fix until the next start

items.reason: these phone files run no scheduled server jobs; the one-time start-up repairs are covered under L6.2
